finding.claim: GET /invoice/<inv_id> has no authentication and no ownership check, so any caller can read any customer's invoice by ID (IDOR). The sibling /my/invoice/<inv_id> enforces inv["customer"] == g.user["id"] at lines 16-17; this route omits it.
finding.source: invoices.py:7-8 - unauthenticated HTTP route; inv_id path parameter
finding.sink: invoices.py:9-10 - INVOICES.get(inv_id) result returned via jsonify(inv)

trace.note: INVOICES.get(inv_id) or abort(404) - lookup only, no customer check
jsonify(inv) returns full record to caller

finding.guards_checked: No auth decorator or before_request hook in this file; no ownership comparison on this path; IDs are plain dict keys (enumerable). Sibling /my/invoice (lines 16-17) does enforce ownership, so the omission is specific to this route. Not verifiable from repo: g.user population (middleware not present), which affects /my/ routes only.

verdict.guard_found: none. invoices.py:7 registers the route with no auth decorator; invoices.py:9 is a bare dict lookup (INVOICES.get) with abort(404) only for a missing key; invoices.py:10 returns the full record. The only ownership check is at invoices.py:16-17, in the separate get_my_invoice route. A grep of the directory found no before_request, before_app_request, login_required, or g.user assignment anywhere that would gate this route.
verdict.reason: Anonymous callers can reach get_invoice at invoices.py:7-10 and read any invoice by ID, since no auth or customer comparison guards the lookup, unlike the sibling route's check at invoices.py:16-17.
